title: Herbarium Specimens Collection and Metadata Entry
author: Sabine St-Jean
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9j8h4rw

steps.title: Gather required equipment and supplies
steps.instruction: Collect the following items before field work: a permanent marker; stake‑wire flags about 50 cm long with 3.5 in × 2.5 in pink or orange vinyl flags on wire stakes (see https://www.homedepot.com/p/Empire-3-5-in-x-2-5-in-Pink-Stake-Flags-100-Pack-78-003/301387971); identification guides; a CAT S41 fieldwork cellphone (https://www.catphones.com/en-us/cat-s41-smartphone/); a Trimble Catalyst GPS with an NTRIP precision subscription; a gardening shovel; Ziploc bags; a plant press and newspaper; ice packs; and a cooler.

steps.title: Create plant record in Fulcrum
steps.instruction: Open Fulcrum, create a new plant record, and assign a unique Tag ID using the format [InitialLastNameResearcher]-[SpeciesLatinName].

steps.title: Enter project and site metadata
steps.instruction: In Fulcrum under Plants → Metadata, select the appropriate project (see Open Vegetation Survey Protocol → Guidelines → Site Specific Information). Then under Plants → Site and Plot, choose the correct site and plot (if applicable). Finally, under Plants → Site Plot Information, select the appropriate site ID.

steps.title: Record tagging status and place stake
steps.instruction: In Plants → Plant answer “Plant Tagged?”. Choose **Yes** if precise georeferencing will not be done immediately (e.g., Trimble GPS unavailable). Mark the plant location with a stake bearing flagging tape labeled with the same Tag ID format, and in Fulcrum enter the Tag ID and select tag type “stake at plant base”. Choose **No** if you will georeference immediately; no stake is needed. Optionally take a photo of the plant and upload it under Plant Photos.

steps.title: Log first occurrence information
steps.instruction: Under Plants → Plant First Occurrence, enter the observer’s name and the observation date (defaults are the logged‑in user and current date).

steps.title: Georeference plant location
steps.instruction: Under Plants → Location, connect the Trimble Catalyst to your cellphone (or use the cellphone GPS if the Trimble is unavailable) and click “Update Location with GPS”. The coordinates will auto‑populate the Latitude and Longitude fields.

steps.title: Select taxon and record identification
steps.instruction: Under Plants → Taxon, select the species. Then under Plants → Taxonomic Identification, record the identifier’s name, the identification date, and the identification protocol (defaults are the logged‑in user and current date).

steps.title: Collect plant specimen and label bag
steps.instruction: Using a gardening shovel, excavate the plant with its roots. Place the specimen in a Ziploc bag labeled with the species Latin name, the plant ID, and the collection date. Remove the stake tag after the specimen is collected.

steps.title: Collect additional specimens outside plots
steps.instruction: Select additional plants outside the surveyed plots that have been identified in at least one vegetation survey. Collect one herbarium specimen per species (more if specimens are small enough to fill a newspaper page). Prioritize completing vegetation surveys, but collect as many surveyed species as possible. Apply the same procedure for unknown plants.

steps.title: Press specimens and label newspaper
steps.instruction: Place the collected specimens in a plant press with newspaper. Label the newspaper with site, collection date, species name, and plant ID. No mounting is required. Follow the guidelines at https://www.herbier.ulaval.ca/en/a_propos/confectionner_un_herbier/.

steps.title: Create pressed‑specimen entry in Fulcrum
steps.instruction: In Fulcrum, go to Pressed Specimens and create an entry for each pressed specimen. Under Metadata → Project select the appropriate project; under Site and Plant → Plant select the corresponding plant. Under Collection Event, enter the collector’s name and the collection date.

steps.title: Transport specimens to herbarium
steps.instruction: Bring the pressed specimens to Montréal’s Botanical Garden for mounting and storage at the Marie‑Victorin Herbarium.

steps.title: Store specimens in cool environment
steps.instruction: Keep specimens in a cooler with ice packs (or another cool environment) between collection and pressing.
